common_name: Mr. Henry Cox Pelargonium (Tricolor Fancy-Leaf Zonal Geranium)

planting.note: Set out after frost danger has passed; grow in containers to overwinter indoors in cold climates. Mr. Henry Cox colors most vividly in bright light with cool nights.

directions: Plant in full sun to light afternoon shade in well-drained soil, letting the top of the soil dry slightly between waterings. Mr. Henry Cox is a Victorian-era tricolor zonal geranium closely related to Mrs. Pollock, its rounded leaves overlaid with bands of gold, sage-green, and a dusky purple-red zone that intensifies in bright light, topped by small single salmon-orange flowers that play a secondary role to the striking foliage. The muted, smoky tone of its central zone distinguishes it from brighter tricolor cultivars, giving it a softer, antique appearance prized in heritage plantings. Pinch stems to keep it bushy, and take cuttings easily to propagate; it is frost-tender, so bring containers indoors to a bright window before the first freeze.

common_name: Caroline Schmidt Pelargonium (White-Edged Double Red Zonal Geranium)

planting.note: Set out after frost danger has passed; grow in containers to overwinter indoors in cold climates.

directions: Plant in full sun to light afternoon shade in well-drained soil, letting the top of the soil dry slightly between waterings. Caroline Schmidt is a classic German heirloom bicolor zonal geranium, its rounded green leaves crisply edged in a wide band of creamy white that stays crisp all season, setting off clusters of fully double, brick-red flowers held well above the foliage. The strong contrast between the variegated leaf margin and the saturated red blooms makes it a standout bedding and container plant even from a distance. Pinch stems to keep it bushy, and take cuttings easily to propagate; it is frost-tender, so bring containers indoors to a bright window before the first freeze.

common_name: Wilhelm Langguth Pelargonium (White-Edged Silver-Leaf Zonal Geranium)

planting.note: Set out after frost danger has passed; grow in containers to overwinter indoors in cold climates.

directions: Plant in full sun to light afternoon shade in well-drained soil, letting the top of the soil dry slightly between waterings. Wilhelm Langguth is a historic German silver-leaf zonal geranium, its narrow, deeply zoned green leaves bordered by a crisp band of white variegation that gives the whole plant a frosted, silvery cast, contrasting with clusters of bright scarlet-red single flowers. Its compact, tidy habit and finely marked foliage make it a long-favored choice for edging and container displays where the leaf pattern can be seen up close. Pinch stems to keep it bushy, and take cuttings easily to propagate; it is frost-tender, so bring containers indoors to a bright window before the first freeze.

common_name: Frank Headley Pelargonium (Cream-Edged Pale Pink Zonal Geranium)

planting.note: Set out after frost danger has passed; grow in containers to overwinter indoors in cold climates.

directions: Plant in full sun to light afternoon shade in well-drained soil, letting the top of the soil dry slightly between waterings. Frank Headley is a dwarf, compact zonal geranium with small grey-green leaves neatly edged in creamy white, a subtle faded zone, and soft pale salmon-pink single flowers that harmonize gently with the muted foliage rather than competing with it. Its small, tidy stature makes it especially well suited to windowsill pots, edging, and small containers where larger zonal cultivars would overwhelm the space. Pinch stems to keep it bushy, and take cuttings easily to propagate; it is frost-tender, so bring containers indoors to a bright window before the first freeze.

common_name: Crystal Palace Gem Pelargonium (Golden Butterfly-Leaf Zonal Geranium)

planting.note: Set out after frost danger has passed; grow in containers to overwinter indoors in cold climates. Foliage color is brightest in strong light.

directions: Plant in full sun to light afternoon shade in well-drained soil, letting the top of the soil dry slightly between waterings. Crystal Palace Gem is a Victorian-era golden-leaf zonal geranium dating to the 1870s, its rounded chartreuse-gold leaves marked by a butterfly-shaped olive-green central zone, topped by clusters of single scarlet-red flowers that stand out sharply against the bright foliage. As one of the oldest continuously grown fancy-leaf pelargonium cultivars, it remains a favorite for heritage gardens and mixed containers seeking bold, sun-loving foliage color. Pinch stems to keep it bushy, and take cuttings easily to propagate; it is frost-tender, so bring containers indoors to a bright window before the first freeze.

common_name: Summer Showers Pelargonium (Variegated Trailing Ivy Geranium)

planting.note: Set out after frost danger has passed; grow in hanging baskets or containers to overwinter indoors in cold climates.

directions: Plant in full sun to light afternoon shade in well-drained soil, letting the top of the soil dry slightly between waterings. Summer Showers is a trailing ivy-leaf geranium with glossy, waxy, ivy-shaped leaves irregularly splashed in cream and pale yellow variegation along green margins, paired with clusters of small lavender-pink flowers on long cascading stems. Its variegated foliage provides interest even when bloom is light, making it a favorite for hanging baskets, window boxes, and spilling over container edges. Pinch trailing stems to encourage branching and take cuttings easily to propagate; it is frost-tender, so bring containers indoors to a bright window before the first freeze.

common_name: Ville de Paris Pelargonium (Semi-Double Pink Trailing Ivy Geranium)

planting.note: Set out after frost danger has passed; grow in hanging baskets or containers to overwinter indoors in cold climates.

directions: Plant in full sun to light afternoon shade in well-drained soil, letting the top of the soil dry slightly between waterings. Ville de Paris is a classic trailing ivy-leaf geranium with glossy, thick, waxy leaves and abundant semi-double soft pink flowers borne in tight clusters along long, cascading stems. Its free-flowering habit and heat tolerance have kept it in cultivation for generations as a hanging basket and window box staple, particularly in European summer bedding displays. Pinch trailing stems to encourage branching and take cuttings easily to propagate; it is frost-tender, so bring containers indoors to a bright window before the first freeze.

common_name: Attar of Roses Geranium (Classic Rose-Scented Pelargonium)

planting.note: Root stem cuttings in spring in full sun to partial shade in well-drained, lean, slightly acidic to neutral soil in zone 9-11; Attar of Roses is one of the oldest and most intensely rose-scented of the scented geraniums, grown historically for perfume-grade rose oil extraction.

directions: Root cuttings in lean, well-drained soil and grow in full sun to partial shade with light, infrequent watering, allowing soil to dry between waterings; overly rich soil or heavy shade will dull the fragrance. Pinch stems regularly to maintain a full, shrubby shape; the deeply cut, velvety grey-green leaves release an intense, sweet rose fragrance at the lightest touch, among the strongest of any rose-scented pelargonium, while small lavender-pink flowers appear in loose clusters but are secondary to the foliage's aromatic value. The leaves are used fresh or dried to flavor sugar, baked goods, jellies, and teas, or historically distilled for rose-scented oil. Bring indoors well before first frost as a houseplant, since it has no cold hardiness.

common_name: Lord Bute Regal Pelargonium (Dark Velvet Maroon Martha Washington Geranium)

planting.note: Set out after frost danger has passed; grow in containers to overwinter indoors in cold climates. Regal pelargoniums like Lord Bute rest and drop leaves in high summer heat and rebloom as temperatures cool.

directions: Plant in full sun to light afternoon shade in well-drained soil, letting the top of the soil dry slightly between waterings, and avoid heavy fertilizing which reduces bloom. Lord Bute is one of the oldest and most famous regal (Martha Washington) pelargonium cultivars, prized for its large, ruffled flowers of an unusually deep maroon-black hue edged in a narrow band of brighter burgundy-red, held above coarsely toothed, dark green leaves in a dense flush of spring bloom. Unlike zonal geraniums, regal types bloom in a concentrated spring-to-early-summer flush and prefer cooler conditions, often resting through peak summer heat before a smaller autumn rebloom. Take cuttings in late summer to propagate; it is frost-tender, so bring containers indoors to a bright, cool spot before the first freeze.

common_name: Catford Belle Angel Pelargonium (Orchid-Pink Viola-Flowered Geranium)

planting.note: Set out after frost danger has passed; grow in containers to overwinter indoors in cold climates.

directions: Plant in full sun to light afternoon shade in well-drained soil, letting the top of the soil dry slightly between waterings. Catford Belle is a classic angel pelargonium, a group bred from regal geranium crosses with a more compact, mounding habit and small, crinkled, scented leaves, bearing abundant small viola-like flowers in orchid-pink with a bold deep maroon blotch on the upper petals. Unlike regal types, angel pelargoniums bloom more continuously through the warm season rather than in a single concentrated flush, making them useful for containers and hanging baskets wanting sustained color. Pinch stems to keep it bushy, and take cuttings easily to propagate; it is frost-tender, so bring containers indoors to a bright window before the first freeze.
